The definition of validation for ML models differs from that for medical devices in that validation in the context of ML is primarily understood as an approach to algorithm tuning, focusing on an unbiased evaluation of model performance to demonstrate appropriate learning algorithm parameter choice. In contrast, validation for medical devices involves confirming that the device meets specified goals and intended purposes, including safety and performance, through a systematic process of clinical evaluation.

The role of clinical evaluation is to continuously generate, collect, analyze, and assess clinical data to verify the safety and performance of a medical device when used as intended. This process is ongoing and includes post-market clinical follow-up, ensuring that the device remains effective and safe over time. Thus, while ML validation is more about model performance and tuning, clinical evaluation is about ensuring that the medical device fulfills its intended use and maintains a state-of-the-art safety profile.
